explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1075. For r ≥ 3 there is c > r^{-r} such that, for every ε > 0, some m(n) → ∞ works: for all large n, every r-uniform hypergraph on Fin n with at least (1+ε)(n/r)^r edges has an m(n)-vertex set S spanning at least c·|S|^r edges (hypergraphInduce keeps the edges contained in S). Letting m depend on ε is the natural reading of 'm = m(n)'. The threshold is meaningful, because the complete balanced r-partite hypergraph has (n/r)^r edges and every m-subset spans at most (m/r)^r of them.
